title: AI vs. AI: Building Resilient Enterprises in the Age of Autonomous Threats

metadata.speaker: Dinis Cruz
metadata.event: Black Hat Europe 2025 - AI Security Summit

slides.title: AI vs. AI
slides.subtitle: Building Resilient Enterprises in the Age of Autonomous Threats

slides.name: DINIS CRUZ
slides.role:
GenAI Entrepreneur & Former CISO
Akeia.ai / The Cyber Boardroom / MyFeeds.ai
slides.notes: Brief introduction - ex-CISO background, now building AI security tools.

slides.title: SECURITY'S FOUR PILLARS - ALL BROKEN

items.label: Engineering & Technology
items.text: We know how to build secure systems - we don't do it at scale

items.label: Business Processes
items.text: Security is an afterthought, not embedded in decisions

items.label: Funding & Focus
items.text: NFRs chronically underfunded - features always win

items.label: Risk Management
items.text: Spreadsheets and heat maps disconnected from technical reality

slides.insight: Systems are insecure not because engineers are stupid, but because the ENVIRONMENT forces corner-cutting. All four pillars must be aligned.

slides.title: WE'VE BEEN GETTING AWAY WITH IT

items.label: AWS
items.text: Timing bug wiped out a global database

items.label: Azure
items.text: Config inconsistency silently propagated, then 'detonated' worldwide

items.label: Cloudflare
items.text: Routine config change crashed bot defense, halted traffic

items.label: CrowdStrike
items.text: 8.5 million Windows systems bricked by a faulty update

slides.insight: These weren't sophisticated attacks - they were minor glitches that cascaded. Now imagine if they were deliberate, coordinated attacks.

slides.title: HUMAN INSIDERS VS. AI AGENTS

items: Natural limitations on skill and time
No moral compass unless explicitly constrained

slides.insight: We've never had a malicious insider that can instantly devise new approaches when initial attempts fail. AI doesn't give up - it gets creative.

slides.title: THREE CATEGORIES OF AI-DRIVEN THREATS

items.label: Malicious AI Agents
items.text: Fully autonomous malware that learns, adapts, and persists

items.label: Compromised Benign Agents
items.text: Your AI bots hijacked via prompt injection - operating with legitimate access, now working for the adversary

items.label: Unintentionally Harmful Agents
items.text: The paperclip maximizer scenario - dangerously efficient in ways we didn't anticipate

slides.insight: Prompt injection remains unsolved - any AI taking untrusted input can be subverted.

slides.title: FRAGILE BY DEFAULT

items.label: Technical Debt Crisis
points: ~40% of IT asset value is technical debt (McKinsey)
Systems running 'hot' with minimal safety margins

items.label: Hidden Interdependencies
points: Internet = circular dependency machine
Identity, DNS, cloud, CDN - one failure cascades globally

items.label: No Visibility, No Recovery
points: Only ~54% have documented DR plans - fewer actually test them
Most can't do surgical rollback - it's full restore or nothing

items.label: No Version Control for Data
points: Code has Git. Databases? Configs? Often nothing.
If an AI corrupts records, can you rewind?

slides.insight: You can't protect what you don't understand. You can't recover what you haven't practiced.

slides.title: THE DEFENDER'S EDGE
slides.subtitle: AI as Force Multiplier, Not Black Box

slides.title: ATTACKERS ALWAYS MAKE MISTAKES

items.label: The '100% Prevention' Myth
points: You cannot patch everything, eliminate every gap
And you don't have to

items.label: Every Attack Has 5-10 Missteps
points: Unusual logins, wrong processes, odd data movement
Attackers lack perfect insider knowledge - they wander, they probe

items.label: Your Job: Catch the Mistakes
points: Before they reach the crown jewels
Whether it's an external attacker OR your own AI spiraling

slides.insight: Perfect prevention is impossible AND unnecessary. Detection and response are the asymmetric advantage.

slides.title: SECURITY'S ASYMMETRIC ADVANTAGE

items.label: Unique Enterprise-Wide Vantage Point
points: Access to every system, every data flow
One of few functions focused on business SURVIVAL, not narrow objectives

items.label: You Know What 'Good' Looks Like
points: You define the baseline - attackers must deviate from it
The moment something acts outside normal, you catch it

items.label: Home Court Advantage
points: Attackers wander chasing dead ends, making noise
You know the terrain - use it

slides.insight: Defenders think in lists, attackers think in graphs. We need to arm defenders with graphs - and the AI to make sense of them.

slides.title: THE MECHANISM: KNOWLEDGE GRAPHS

items.label: Build a Digital Twin of Your Enterprise
points: Systems, data flows, identities, dependencies - all connected
Not static docs - a living, queryable model

items.label: Semantic Graphs Link Everything
points: Each team's data model connects to the whole
Query: 'What breaks if System X goes down?' - instant answer

items.label: AI Builds and Maintains the Graph
points: LLMs digest docs, configs, logs into structure
Humans make decisions, AI updates the map continuously

slides.insight: Use GenAI to BUILD the knowledge, but use deterministic systems for real-time enforcement. The graph is your situational awareness.

slides.title: ASSUME COMPROMISE, CONTAIN BLAST RADIUS

items.label: Strong Segmentation Inside
points: Crown-jewel systems walled off with strict controls
One-way isolation for legacy components that can't be fixed

items.label: Graceful Degradation = Victory
points: Parts may fail, but they fail SAFELY
No cascade into total enterprise collapse

items.label: Hardened Boundaries Around What Can't Be Fixed
points: API throttles for fragile older systems
Circuit breakers that halt abnormal transactions automatically

slides.insight: Every agent you add to mission-critical systems becomes part of your attack surface. Simplify first.

slides.title: VERSION CONTROL EVERYTHING

items.label: Code Has Git. What About Data?
points: If an AI corrupts your database, can you rewind?
Most orgs: No version history, no audit trail, no rollback

items.label: Immutable Logs, Append-Only Where Possible
points: Every change recorded and reversible
Tampering becomes evident because history can't be rewritten

items.label: Consider File System as Database
points: Simpler architecture = smaller attack surface
Standard backup/versioning tools work out of the box

slides.insight: SBOMs act like Git commits for software. Extend that concept to ALL enterprise data.

slides.title: IDENTITY GRAPHS: LEAST PRIVILEGE AT SCALE

items.label: Map Every Identity and Permission
points: Users, services, AI agents - all in one graph
Query: 'If this account is compromised, what can it reach?'

items.label: Just-in-Time, Just-Enough Access
points: Privileges that EXPIRE, not persist
Admin rights only when explicitly unlocked, auto-revoke after

items.label: Shrink the Blast Radius
points: One compromised account ≠ full breach
Attacker hits walls immediately - can't pivot everywhere

slides.insight: Identity is the new perimeter. Zero Trust isn't a product - it's this architecture.

slides.title: FUND NFRs AT UNPRECEDENTED SCALE

items.label: Test Your Recovery - For Real
points: Backup drills that actually restore, not just 'assume it works'
Chaos engineering beyond normal peaks - AI hammers APIs 24/7

items.label: Instrument Everything
points: Real-time visibility into what's happening across systems
If it isn't measured, it doesn't get managed - or funded

items.label: Simplify Ruthlessly
points: Consolidate workflows - 7 microservices → 3 on one platform
Pause new AI deployments until the foundation can support them

items.label: Demand Vendor Accountability
points: The market doesn't currently punish fragility - change that in contracts
Require SBOMs, security labels, evidence of secure development

slides.insight: Every dollar spent upfront on NFRs saves many dollars in incident response. If it isn't required in contracts, it doesn't get done.
slides.notes: NFRs: scalability, fault tolerance, observability, recoverability, documentation, maintainability. Chronically under-funded because they're invisible until failure.

slides.title: VIBE CODING: THE NEW SPREADSHEETS

items.label: Creating Software Is Now Trivially Easy
points: Non-engineers building apps via AI prompts
If the software doesn't exist, they will it into existence over coffee

items.label: Same Pattern as Excel - On Steroids
points: Solves immediate problem brilliantly
Becomes mission-critical overnight with zero governance

items.label: Shadow AI Is Already Here
points: Employees pasting sensitive data into ChatGPT daily
Department-level AI tools running under IT's radar

slides.insight: Just like spreadsheets couldn't be banned, vibe coding won't be stopped. The question isn't IF but HOW you govern it.

slides.title: DON'T BECOME THE DEPARTMENT OF 'NO'

items.label: The Horse Has Bolted
points: Employees will use AI regardless of policy
Shadow-IT AI is far worse than governed AI

items.label: Security as Enabler and Guide
points: Provide vetted platforms and clear guidelines
Build safe internal AI services before they run to ChatGPT

items.label: Create Handoff Pathways
points: Pair business 'vibe coders' with engineering buddies
When a prototype gets traction, help industrialize it safely

slides.insight: We did this for cloud - shifted from 'no cloud' to 'here's a secure cloud framework'. Time to do it again for GenAI.

slides.title: THE PATH FORWARD
slides.subtitle: From Reactive Firefighting to Proactive Containment

slides.title: CALL TO ACTION

items.label: Build Your Digital Twin Now
points: Knowledge graphs of your enterprise - don't wait for a crisis

items.label: Invest in Detection Over Prevention
points: Catch the 5-10 mistakes attackers will make

items.label: Simplify Ruthlessly
points: Every agent you add is attack surface - earn its place

items.label: Version Control EVERYTHING
points: Data, configs, permissions - if you can't rewind, you can't recover

items.label: Enable, Don't Block
points: Govern vibe coding before it governs you

slides.insight: The side that UNDERSTANDS faster wins. Not the side that deploys more AI.
